model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between the Co-occurrence Number and ACC (%) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis represents the Co-occurrence Number on a logarithmic scale, with visible tick labels at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis represents ACC (%), utilizing a linear scale with tick marks ranging from 40 to 65 at a regular interval of 5 units. The plot features six solid lines, each corresponding to a different method and distinguished by color and marker shape, with all lines exhibiting an increasing trend across four plotted data points along the x-axis. The black line for "Base" with circular markers starts at an initial y-value of approximately 38% and steadily increases to end at roughly 44%. The blue line for "FT" with downward-pointing triangle markers begins near 40% and rises steadily to about 48% at the final data point. The red line for "IKE" with upward-pointing triangle markers starts at around 43% and ascends to finish near 49.5%. The brown line for "MEND" with diamond markers starts at roughly 44.5% and climbs steadily to end at approximately 56.5%. The purple line for "MEMIT" with pentagon markers initiates at roughly 43.5%, rises sharply to approximately 51% at its second data point, and then increases more gradually to finish near 54.5%. Finally, the green line for "ROME" with square markers starts at the highest initial value of about 51% and maintains a steady upward trend to finish at approximately 66%.
